title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after the deterministic validator and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute reduction = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported. We (1) correct contingency-cell labeling and map it to archived CSVs, (2) explain provider-call accounting and why model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair), and (3) document unresolved reviewer requests that cannot be resolved from the supplied artifacts (per-vendor breakdown and explicit discordant-episode identifier). All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 digests referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Motivation. Translating human intent into device-specific network configuration via LLMs is attractive for NetOps automation but raises operational risk: syntactic, semantic, and policy violations in generated configs can cause outages. Deterministic validators and automated repairs are common guardrails, yet quantified marginal benefit of such guards under preregistered confirmatory conditions is scarce. Research question. After autonomy-locked preregistration we asked: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and which residual error types remain after automated repairs? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001) executed end-to-end with archived artifacts and cryptographic hashes; (2) a compact, artifact-grounded correction of contingency-cell labeling and provider-call accounting; (3) a null/near-null confirmatory outcome for the chosen model/validator/task bank and an explicit statement of unresolved reviewer requests that cannot be satisfied from the supplied evidence.
sections.related_work: We build on deterministic network verification and runtime checkers (e.g., header-space analyses and incremental checkers) and on recent LLM→NetOps evaluations and prototypes (NetConfEval and intent-driven configuration studies). Our study differs by (a) preregistering a paired confirmatory estimand, (b) forcing a small repair budget (≤1 automated repair per task) via an adapter contract, and (c) archiving the complete execution/analysis artifacts with SHA-256 digests to support forensic inspection.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The preregistration (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) froze a paired binary design (N=200 tasks, stratified sampling planned across three vendor families) and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Adapter contract and model. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Maximum_model_calls = 400; actual model_calls_used recorded = 201 (see reconciliation below). Generation semantics and provider-call accounting (clarification). The pipeline used a shared_initial_candidate per task (independent_condition_generation = false). For each task the baseline label applies to that shared_initial candidate. The guarded artifact is the final artifact after validator+repair when repair was invoked; if no repair was invoked guarded==shared_initial. Provider_call_audit in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}, which yields model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair. Repair-invocation policy and enforcement. The adapter enforced maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (preregistered). The adapter invoked an automated repair only when the deterministic validator reported the shared_initial candidate as invalid (validator field validation_before.valid == false / violation_count > 0). The provider_call_audit confirms that the adapter enforced the maximum: stage_counts shows a single repair call across all tasks. Validator and scoring. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performed canonical parsing, intent-constraint checks, dependency/workflow checks, and simulator-based semantic checks. Each episode produced an archived per-task JSON trace under execution/scoring/ with fields validation_before, validation_after, violation_count, normalized_configuration, and score (0/1). Missingness and exclusions. The preregistered retry and missingness policy was applied; no model-call failures occurred and complete_pairs = 200 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00ef1a906db9c3422947d9bb9997089bbebbf3c9ebc731353240265c1c).
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcome. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 on archived scoring JSONs (input results SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (baseline success rate = 0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (guarded success rate = 1.000). Absolute paired reduction (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Discordant-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Statistical tests. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the absolute reduction = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Contingency-cell notation (corrected). The archived CSV header ordering is 'guarded,baseline,count' (guarded first, baseline second). We define n_11 as guarded=1 & baseline=1, n_10 as guarded=1 & baseline=0 (guarded-only improvements), n_01 as guarded=0 & baseline=1 (baseline-only), and n_00 as guarded=0 & baseline=0. In this run the single discordant cell is n_10 = 1, i.e., an improvement (baseline-invalid → guarded-valid). Forensic retrieval of discordant episode. The raw paired episode records and per-episode scoring JSONs are archived under execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) and execution/scoring/*.json (artifact hashes cited in the Disclosure Statement). The supplied manuscript evidence bundle does not contain the explicit single discordant episode identifier in the manuscript text; auditors can locate the episode id by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for the record where baseline score == 0 and guarded score == 1. Secondary preregistered hypothesis (H2) status. H2 (residual-error-type contingency) could not be executed as a confirmatory test because there are no guarded residual actionable failures (n_01 + n_00 = 0). Any error-type commentary is therefore exploratory only.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. Under the constrained experimental conditions (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, single deterministic validator implementation, and an adapter-enforced single-repair budget), the guarded pipeline yielded only a numerically small absolute reduction because baseline LLM-generated actionable-error prevalence was already extremely low (1/200). Operational implications. Deterministic validators remain valuable for canonicalization, auditability, and surfacing systematic failure clusters; their realized operational ROI depends on baseline generator accuracy, validator coverage, repair budget, and costs of human review. Study limitations that affect interpretation and reviewer requests. (1) Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; no multi-model generality is implied. (2) Synthetic benchmark and validator scope: task realism and validator semantics bound external validity. (3) Low baseline error prevalence limits power to detect moderate relative improvements in rare-failure regimes. (4) Repair budget: adapter enforced ≤1 repair per task (provider_call_audit stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":200, "repair":1}; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). (5) Reviewer-requested per-vendor stratified contingency counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier are not present in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle in textual form; they can be computed by auditors from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 provided) and execution/scoring/*.json, but we do not invent or publish a specific per-vendor table or episode id because those values are not present verbatim in the archived manuscript bundle supplied for revision. This unresolved reviewer request is recorded transparently rather than fabricated. Reproducibility. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts referenced above are archived with SHA-256 checksums and explicit file paths (see Disclosure Statement).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment of a deterministic-validator guard for LLM→NetOps generate→verify→repair pipelines. On the chosen synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator/repair adapter (≤1 repair), the absolute actionable-misconfiguration reduction was 0.005 (from 1/200 to 0/200). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported. We corrected contingency-cell labeling, clarified provider-call accounting (model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair), documented the adapter's repair-invocation enforcement (max 1 repair; repair invoked on validator-detected invalid shared_initial candidates), and preserved reviewer requests that cannot be resolved from the supplied artifacts as explicit unresolved items for auditors. Future work should expand model coverage, validator implementations, repair budgets, and task realism to identify regimes where validator-assisted repair yields material operational risk reduction.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-required per-vendor stratified counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 provided) and execution/scoring/*.json but we do not invent or assert specific per-vendor numbers or an episode id in the manuscript where they are not present in the supplied archive.
